html:
Kuomboka is the ceremony in which the king of the Lozi moves from his palace on the Zambezi floodplain to higher ground when the river floods, usually in March or April.

The Litunga travels in the royal barge, the Nalikwanda, painted black and white with a great elephant on top and paddled by about a hundred men, while drums sound and thousands watch from canoes and the banks. The journey takes most of a day.

It marks how life in Barotseland follows the flood, which feeds the grazing and fishing of the plain. The ceremony draws visitors from across Zambia and abroad. The flood plain is part of the Zambezi system.
sum: Kuomboka is the ceremony in which the king of the Lozi moves from his palace on the Zambezi floodplain to higher ground when the river floods, usually in March or April.
